b: Which feature makes translation chemically different from transcription?

Complementary base pairing alone directly forms peptide bonds|It maps nucleotide triplets to amino-acid residues through molecular adaptors|It copies an RNA into another RNA|It always begins at the transcription +1 site
Translation connects two chemically distinct polymers via charged tRNAs. Complementary copying describes transcription, not peptide synthesis; the initiation site of translation is distinct from +1.
Under a fixed-length four-letter code, why are two-letter words insufficient for 20 amino acids?
There are 8 words|There are 16 words|There are 20 words but no stops|All words must contain different bases
4² = 16. Repeated letters are allowed and positions are independent. A three-letter alphabet has 64 words.
Which statement correctly distinguishes degeneracy from ambiguity?
A codon normally directs several different residues|Every amino acid has six codons|Several distinct codons can specify one residue|Each sense codon is read by exactly one tRNA
Degeneracy is many-to-one mapping. It does not require equal degeneracy, one tRNA per codon, or multiple ordinary amino-acid assignments per codon.
Which standard-code amino-acid pair has one codon each?
Met and Trp|Lys and Glu|Ile and Val|Ser and Arg
AUG and UGG are the single ordinary sense assignments for methionine and tryptophan. The other residues have multiple codons.
A codon written 5′-GAC-3′ has which strictly complementary anticodon written 5′ to 3′?
CUG|GUC|CAG|GAC
The aligned anticodon is 3′-CUG-5′; reverse it to obtain 5′-GUC-3′. CUG is the correct complement only in the opposite orientation.
In conventional tRNA numbering, which position faces codon base 3?
The interaction is antiparallel: 36 faces 1, 35 faces 2, and 34 faces 3. Position 73 lies near the acceptor end, not the anticodon.
Under classical wobble rules, which codon endings can anticodon position 34 G recognize?
A and G|U and C|A and C|All four
G pairs canonically with C and by wobble with U. U at position 34 recognizes A/G in the simplified model.
An anticodon 5′-IAU-3′ recognizes which standard sense family in the classical model?
AUG only|AUU, AUC and AUA|UAU, UAC and UAA|All four AU codons
The fixed first two codon bases are AU; I recognizes U/C/A, not G in this model. The three targets specify isoleucine.
Which statement about AUG is correct?
Every AUG begins a separate protein|An internal AUG normally encodes methionine|AUG is a stop signal in all bacteria|AUG cannot be used by an initiator tRNA
Internal AUG normally directs methionine incorporation, while initiation requires a suitable context and initiator tRNA. Identical triplets need not act as starts.
An experimentally established bacterial GUG initiation site usually gives which initial residue?
Valine|Leucine|N-formylmethionine|Glycine
GUG can serve as a start recognized by the bacterial initiator fMet-tRNA. Internal GUG normally specifies valine.
Which three are conventional standard stop codons?
UAA, UAG, UGA|AUG, UAA, UGG|UAC, UAU, UAA|UGU, UGC, UGG
UAA, UAG and UGA normally signal termination. AUG specifies methionine, UGG tryptophan, UAU/UAC tyrosine and UGU/UGC cysteine.
Which conclusion is justified by a poly(U)-directed polyphenylalanine product in a triplet framework?
All U-containing codons specify phenylalanine|UUU specifies phenylalanine|Poly(U) establishes all codon boundaries by itself|UUU is a start codon in normal cells
Every complete triplet in a poly(U) template is UUU. The result identifies that assignment in the triplet framework, but a homopolymer alone cannot establish word length.
What was the distinctive contribution of Nirenberg and Leder's defined-trinucleotide assay?
It measured transcription start positions|It linked a particular ordered triplet to aminoacyl-tRNA binding on ribosomes|It proved every gene has one exon|It sequenced whole proteins directly
The assay tested ordered triplets through specific ribosome-associated aminoacyl-tRNA retention; it did not require full-length peptide synthesis.
Which experimental observation supported a three-nucleotide reading phase in the T4 rII study?
Every substitution was lethal|Certain combinations of three same-sign frame changes restored function|Only poly(U) bound ribosomes|All mutant genomes were identical in sequence
Restoration of reading phase by combinations of frame changes supported a triplet code. Functional compensation did not imply restoration of the original sequence.
Which change is synonymous under the standard internal code?
GAA→GAG|GAA→GUA|GAA→UAA|GAA→GCA
GAA/GAG encode Glu; GUA encodes Val, UAA is stop, and GCA encodes Ala.
A one-nucleotide deletion within a continuous coding region generally causes what consequence?
A one-residue deletion with all downstream codons unchanged|A shift in downstream grouping|A necessary synonymous substitution|A guaranteed increase in protein length
A deletion not divisible by three changes grouping downstream. The new stop and length depend on the actual sequence.
Which distinguishes a three-base deletion from a one-base deletion?

A three-base deletion always leaves the entire protein sequence unchanged|A three-base deletion preserves downstream reading phase, assuming unchanged initiation|A one-base deletion never changes a stop|Both necessarily remove exactly one residue
Three is divisible by the codon length. Junction residues may still change, so phase preservation is not identity of protein sequence.
Which standard-code codon becomes Trp in the vertebrate mitochondrial table?
UAA|UGA|AUA|AGA
UGA is assigned Trp in table 2. AUA is Met, and AGA is listed as termination in that table.
Which statement about selenocysteine is correct?

Every UGA in every cell encodes Sec|Selected UGA codons can encode Sec with specialized machinery and RNA context|Sec is always added to a protein after translation|Sec introduces a fifth ordinary mRNA base
Selective UGA recoding requires a dedicated system and contextual signals. Ordinary termination remains possible at other UGA codons.
What distinguishes programmed ribosomal frameshifting from a DNA frameshift indel?
The RNA sequence need not change|It always requires addition of a DNA nucleotide|The genetic code becomes doublet|It changes every transcript from a genome
Programmed frameshifting alters the ribosome's grouping phase on an existing message; an indel changes the underlying sequence.
A peptide ends with lysine in the nascent chain. Which statement about its following ordinary stop is correct?
The stop contributes another amino acid|The stop specifies release rather than an incorporated residue|The stop is always UGA|The stop must lie in the 5′ UTR
The stop is an in-frame termination signal, not a residue. Any of the three standard stop codons can serve, depending on the sequence.
Why does an ORF prediction alone not establish that a protein is expressed?
ORFs have no triplets|A candidate frame can exist without biological initiation or detectable translation|Every ORF is always a noncoding RNA|All ORFs must contain introns
Sequence-based criteria identify potential coding regions; expression requires supporting biological evidence.
A tRNA has a correct glycine-recognizing anticodon but carries alanine. What follows if it is accepted and used?
Glycine is obligatorily delivered|Alanine can be incorporated at a glycine codon|The mRNA sequence changes|The ribosome necessarily reverses direction
The amino acid delivered depends on the attached residue. The tRNA's anticodon can still recognize the codon correctly; charging and decoding are separate specificity layers.
Which pair shares a standard first-two-base box but encodes different amino acids?
GCU and GCC|UUU and UUA|AAA and AAG|CGU and CGC
UUU is Phe and UUA is Leu. The other pairs are synonymous.
Why is a synonymous substitution not guaranteed to be phenotypically neutral?

It necessarily alters the side chain|It can alter RNA properties or translation efficiency despite preserving the primary sequence|It always deletes three bases|It changes all future codon assignments
The code predicts residue identity, not every aspect of expression. RNA structure, decoding availability and other processes may differ.
Which change is a standard stop-loss mutation?
UAU→UAA|UAG→UGG|GCU→GCC|AAG→AAC
UAG normally terminates, while UGG encodes Trp. UAU→UAA is stop gain; GCU→GCC is synonymous; AAG→AAC is missense.
ar: Different codons can specify the same amino acid.
Both are true; the reason defines degeneracy directly.
The transcription start site and translation start site must always be the same nucleotide.
An mRNA can contain a 5′ untranslated region before its initiation codon.
Assertion false; reason true. The UTR makes the separation explicit.
A single codon substitution does not ordinarily shift the reading frame.
Substitution does not change the number of nucleotides in the sequence.
Both true; the unchanged length preserves phase when initiation and decoding mode are unchanged.
The genetic code is absolutely universal.
UGA has a tryptophan assignment in vertebrate mitochondria.
Assertion false; reason true. Alternative translation tables establish near, not absolute, universality.
An in-frame stop triplet normally adds no amino acid.
Ordinary release factors promote termination instead of an ordinary aminoacyl-tRNA supplying a residue.
Both true; the mechanism explains why the stop is excluded from the nascent chain length.
m: Match: (i) UGG (ii) GCU (iii) UAA (iv) AUA to standard assignments.
Trp, Ala, stop, Ile|Trp, Gly, Lys, Met|Stop, Ala, Trp, Ile|Trp, Ala, Ile, stop
UGG=Trp, GCU=Ala, UAA=stop, AUA=Ile. Mitochondrial AUA is not the standard assignment.

Select the correct statements: (i) 61 sense triplets in the standard code; (ii) all three stop triplets encode residues; (iii) codon position 3 faces tRNA position 34; (iv) a 3′ UTR follows the translated region in a typical mRNA.
i and ii|i, iii and iv|ii and iii|all four
Statements i, iii and iv are correct. Stop triplets ordinarily specify release, not additional residues.
c: A mature mRNA begins translation at coordinate 17. Identify the codon number and position of nucleotide 46.
Codon 10, third base
46−17=29=9×3+2. With one-based indexing, codon=9+1=10 and position=2+1=3. Coordinate 47 begins codon 11.
An uninterrupted coding region including its only terminal stop is 1,203 nt. How many nascent residues and peptide bonds?
400 residues; 399 peptide bonds
1,203/3=401 triplets; subtract one stop gives 400 residues. A linear 400-residue chain contains 399 peptide bonds.
How many sense-region strings encode Met-Ala-Gly-Lys-Trp under independent standard synonymous choices? Include a free conventional stop as a second answer.
32 without stop; 96 including stop
1×4×4×2×1=32. There are three independent stop choices, so 32×3=96.
A toy random RNA has independent equiprobable bases. What is the probability that five consecutive codons contain no standard stop?
There are 61 sense triplets out of 64. Multiply the independent five sense probabilities. This is conditional on a fixed frame, not a probability of actual protein expression.
A random RNA has independent frequencies A=U=0.30, G=C=0.20. Find the probability of a standard stop in a specified triplet.
P(UAA)=0.30×0.30×0.30=0.027; P(UAG)=P(UGA)=0.018. The three mutually exclusive probabilities sum to 0.063.
For GAA, assume each of the nine single-nucleotide alternatives is equally likely. Find the probabilities of synonymous, missense and stop gain.
1/9, 7/9, 1/9 respectively
GAG is synonymous; UAA is stop. AAA, CAA, GCA, GGA, GUA, GAC and GAU are missense. Equal mutation rates are an explicit artificial assumption.
A continuous coding region experiences an insertion of two nucleotides followed by a deletion of five. Is downstream phase restored?
Yes, net −3 nucleotides
2−5=−3, divisible by 3. Grouping after the last event aligns with the original; intermediate residues and termination may have changed.
An RNA is an unlimited repeat of a five-base pattern. How many codons are required before the same position within the repeat recurs?
Five codons
The smallest q satisfying 3q divisible by 5 is 5. The result describes grouping; a real stop codon could prevent completion of the cycle.
A chain has 230 residues and an assumed mean residue mass of 110 Da. Estimate its mass and minimum sense coding length.
230×110=25,300 Da; 230×3=690 nt. Including an ordinary stop gives 693 nt. The mass is approximate and excludes added modifications.
Assume classical wobble coverage for one fourfold, one threefold and one twofold synonymous group in separate first-two-base boxes. Minimum anticodon types?
Four

Two types cover the fourfold box, one inosine type covers U/C/A in the threefold box, and one compatible type covers the twofold group. The calculation assumes the groups have the appropriate endings.
Translate the template DNA written 5′-TTA TGG AAA GTC CAT-3′ assuming a complete standard coding region.
Met-Asp-Phe-Pro
Reverse-complement into mRNA 5′-AUG GAC UUU CCA UAA-3′. Read the four sense codons, then stop.
A sequence is 5′-AUG GCU AAA CCG UAA-3′. Remove the initial G of GCU. Translate every complete displayed codon.
Met-Leu-Asn-Arg; termination not established
The altered sequence groups AUG-CUA-AAC-CGU-AA. The remaining AA is incomplete. The old stop is no longer in phase; downstream sequence is needed to predict eventual termination.
Two coding exons contribute AUGGC and UAAAUAA in their RNA order. What is the spliced coding product?
Met-Ala-Lys
Join to AUGGCUAAAUAA, regroup AUG-GCU-AAA-UAA. GCU crosses the junction; independent exon translation would fail.
Compare standard and vertebrate mitochondrial translation of AUG-AUA-UGA-GCU-UAA, with AUG stipulated as the start.
Standard: Met-Ile; vertebrate mitochondrial: Met-Met-Trp-Ala
In standard decoding AUA is Ile and UGA stops. In table 2 AUA is Met and UGA is Trp; termination is at UAA.
Hypothetical binding assay: labelled Phe-tRNA retention is 30 without triplet, 850 with UUU, and 35 with GCU. What is the strongest inference and one critical control?
UUU specifically promotes Phe-tRNA association with ribosomes; include a no-ribosome control

The large specific increase supports recognition rather than general nucleotide binding. No-ribosome retention assesses nonspecific filter binding. A full synthesis assay would additionally test incorporation.
Hypothetical reporter signals for wild type, +1, +2 and +3 insertions are 100, 3, 2 and 72. What does the pattern support, and what does 72 not prove?
Triplet-phase restoration; not complete restoration of original protein
Three added bases preserve downstream phase. Activity recovery can coexist with altered junction residues, changes in abundance or partial loss of function.
A 5′-IGC-3′ anticodon loses its inosine modification and now contains A at position 34. Predict the simple-model targets before and after.
GCU/GCC/GCA before; GCU after
I34 permits U/C/A; A34 pairs with U. Other tRNAs may compensate in a cell, so reduced recognition range is more certain than the whole-cell phenotype.
A reporter has a premature UAG. A suppressor tRNA restores full-length product but activity remains 20% of wild type. Explain.
Decoding may continue with a wrong residue or inefficient suppression; length alone does not establish normal function
Sequence the product at the suppressed site and quantify full-length abundance. A changed residue or lower yield can account for reduced activity. The DNA mutation need not be repaired.
Hypothetical reporters contain an identical internal UGA; only one has a functional SECIS. Full-length protein occurs chiefly with SECIS. What conclusion is supported, and what needs testing?
Context-dependent readthrough/recoding is supported; verify Sec identity and dependence on the specialized machinery
The contextual signal argues against a universal sense assignment in that system. Product length alone cannot identify the inserted residue.
A synonymous GCU→GCC variant has unchanged mRNA abundance but half the steady-state protein level. Is a missense mechanism supported? Which measurements help?
No conventional missense effect; measure newly synthesized protein and protein turnover
Both encode Ala. Altered initiation/elongation or degradation can change accumulation. Equal steady-state RNA does not prove equal protein production.
Ribosome footprints show phase 0 upstream, phase +1 downstream. Mutation of a candidate signal removes the shift. Is programmed frameshifting proved?
Supported, not conclusively proved
Check mapping, potential overlapping ORFs and actual peptide sequence. The signal-sensitive phase change is compatible with programmed frameshifting but is not uniquely diagnostic.
A bacterial expression construct containing a eukaryotic genomic gene produces an aberrant peptide. Why does standard-code conservation not rule this out?
RNA processing and expression contexts differ between organisms

Introns may be retained in a bacterial transcript; promoters, initiation signals and tRNA availability can differ. The shared code only ensures ordinary assignment given the proper message and context.
A UAU codon is changed to UAG in a vertebrate nuclear gene. A second mutation converts UAG to UAC. Classify both changes relative to their immediate precursor and compare final product with original.
First stop gain; second stop loss; final Tyr restored
UAU and UAC both specify Tyr. UAG is stop. The final local assignment matches wild type, despite a changed nucleotide sequence; expression effects remain possible.
